title: Ask Kurenai's 'In your Journal ›' saves the reply to the Journal again: the button keeps its Save listener, and the real Journal already holds one such duplicate
detail: Copy account: the Mind Journal (kurenai-os-mind) holds 4 entries, two of them identical — same kind (reflection), same title hash and same 605-character text hash, src {kurenai, check}, lesson F1.1 — saved 8 s apart on 21 Nov. Reproduced on the copy offline with KOS.ai.chat stubbed (no model reached; the stub entries deleted afterwards): KOS.mindRun.ask({lesson:'F1.1', mode:'check'}) › Send › '≋ Save to Journal' → 1 new entry and the button reads 'In your Journal ›'; 600 ms later press 'In your Journal ›' → the sheet closes, #/mind/journal opens, and a SECOND identical entry is stored (run 3). Run 1: two presses at once → 2 entries; run 2: presses 50 ms apart, the label had already changed at 2 ms → 2 entries. So the 8 s gap in the real data is the user pressing 'In your Journal ›' to go and read it. The Mind dialogue's end card (mindrun.js:193-197, 'Dialogue: …' reflections) has the same pattern. Invariant 139 keeps the Journal private and local first; a copy also replicates to kos_mind.
rootCause: js/modules/mindrun.js:337-345 — the save button is built with el(..., {onclick: save}), and el() binds 'on*' attributes with addEventListener (js/core/ui.js:48); on success the code sets save.onclick = open-the-Journal (:342), which ADDS a second handler instead of replacing the first, so every later press runs KOS.mindJournal.add again (js/core/mindjournal.js:96, a new id each time). Same at js/modules/mindrun.js:197 for the dialogue's saveBtn.
evidence: /Users/fj/Developer/KurenaiOS-519/audit-evidence/2026-12/shots/copy/mi-dup.js, mi-dup2.js, mi-dup3.js (eval results: after 2, labelBetween 'In your Journal ›', afterFirst 1, cleaned true); IndexedDB kurenai-os-mind entries: 4, two with equal text and title hashes 8 s apart (counts and hashes only, no text read out); js/modules/mindrun.js:342, :197; js/core/ui.js:48
fix: Keep one handler and branch on a saved flag (var savedId = null; onclick: if (savedId) open Journal else add…), or replace the node / removeEventListener; disable the button while the write is pending. Same for the dialogue's saveBtn.

title: Mind card review: 'This deck · 10 due · 10 learnt' counts cards never reviewed as learnt
detail: Copy account: 10 Mind card records; 6 were rated once (22 Nov), 4 were only introduced by finishing a lesson (reps 0, no last review, due 23 Nov). #/mind/cards at mac and iPhone reads 'THIS DECK 10 due · 10 learnt', and those four cards show as due reviews although they have never been seen in a review. The flashcard engine's 'new' count is for exactly these. Reproduced twice (mac, iPhone).
rootCause: js/engines/flashcards.js:301-305 counts any card whose schedule has a due date as learnt; js/core/mind.js:222-228 introduce() gives a lesson's cards a record {due: tomorrow, reps: 0} at once, and mind.js's adapter peek (js/modules/mind.js:916-930) passes that due through.
fix: In the Mind adapter's peek return due only once reps + lapses > 0 (the card counts as new until first rated), or let the engine count 'learnt' by views, not by due.
